title: Runtime midweek synthesis — Oct 05 2026
summary: Midweek capture of ongoing kernel and KV cache work. Focus this week: stabilizing segmented-KV TTL, validating dynamic batch autosizing under p95 burst, and isolating a perf regression seen after kernel F9 merge. Contains experiment notes, blockers, and short-term rollout plan.
body:
Context:
- Purpose: capture asynchronous updates for the serving-runtime squad (kernel, KV cache, batching) so oncall and adjacent teams have a single snapshot midweek.
- Meeting cadence: informal sync + async updates; this doc collects status and handoffs.

Attendees / contributors:
- Maya Chen (owner) — coordinating rollout + QA sampling
- Arjun Patel — kernel patches and microbench artifacts
- Sofia Martinez — KV cache experiments and metrics analysis
- Ben Gallagher — loadbench and A/B runner
- Evelyn Park — SRE/observability hooks, tracing correlation
- Luis Ortega — rollout/infra and canary automation

What changed since last week:
1) Kernel F9 merge (Arjun): merged Friday evening into main, includes a new attention kernel selection heuristic that picks single-pass FusedAttention for short-context requests. Initial microbench looked good with 5-8% p50 improvement, but live experiments show a p99 uplift on some request shapes.
2) Segmented-KV TTL (Sofia): landed an opt-in prototype that shards prefix KVs by session age buckets (0-1m, 1-10m, 10m+) to reduce cache churn for high-fanout sessions. Default is off; tests enabled in canary.
3) Dynamic batch autosizer (Ben): introduced a smoothing factor and max-batch cap of 64; new heuristic respects latency SLOs by scaling batch size down when queueing time exceeds 15ms.

Observed signals and anomalies:
- Regression: since kernel F9 merged, two customers reported spikes in tail latency for short prompts (~32 tokens) at p99. Preliminary trace shows increased scheduler preemption leading to longer queuing for high-concurrency nodes.
- KV cache hit rate: segmented-KV in canary saw a modest hit-rate increase (+3.2%) for demo traffic but also an increase in small object allocations; memory jitter observed on one canary host.
- Batch sizing: dynamic autosizer reduced average cost-per-token by ~6% in loadbench, but under bursty arrival patterns (p95 bursts) we saw ephemeral oversizing that pushed latency over SLO in one test.

Experiments in-flight (details):
A. Kernel fallback window (Arjun) — SR-1197
- Goal: add a traffic-aware fallback so nodes detecting >5% preemption events in 1m window revert to previous kernel path.
- Status: PR open (see linked_artifacts). Running canary for 12h with synthetic short prompts. Observed preemption events lowered by 70% in canary when fallback triggered.
- Risk: adds switching overhead; need to validate KV cache compatibility during kernel flips.

B. Segmented-KV memory cap and slab tuning (Sofia)
- Goal: mitigate small-object jitter by limiting bucket growth and applying slab reuse for commonly sized entries.
- Status: new allocator patch pushed to canary host image; telemetry added to track slab reuse rate.
- Early results: slab reuse at ~82%, memory variance down ~18% in canary.

C. Batch autosizer smoothing factor sweep (Ben)
- Goal: find smoothing alpha that balances reactiveness and stability under p95 bursts. Testing alphas [0.1, 0.25, 0.5].
- Status: alpha=0.25 shows best tradeoff in lab loadbench; will try alpha=0.25 in one canary cluster overnight.

Decisions made this week:
- Pause wide rollout of Kernel F9 for clusters serving mixed short/long prompt workloads until fallback window is enabled. (Reason: prevent customer-impacting p99 regressions.)
- Enable segmented-KV with memory cap = 1.5x baseline on non-production clusters for two full days to collect more signals.
- Tune batch autosizer default smoothing to 0.25 in staging; hold production change until canary confirms.

Blockers and open questions:
- Root cause for scheduler preemption spike not fully identified. Trace correlation suggests a specific microkernel path under contention; need deeper perf counters from impacted hosts (Evelyn to coordinate).
- KV eviction chatter: why some sessions show large eviction storms when segmented buckets rotate. Hypothesis: uneven session distribution across buckets. Need a sampling job to reconstruct session age histograms.
- Can we instrument kernel switch events in a way that does not add >1% CPU overhead? (Tradeoff between observability and perturbation.)

Short-term action items (owners + ETA):
- Add preemption perf counters to canary hosts and collect 6h of data (Evelyn Park) — due 2026-10-06
- Implement kernel fallback window threshold as a config flag and deploy to canary (Arjun Patel) — due 2026-10-06
- Ramp segmented-KV on two additional non-prod clusters and enable slab allocator patch (Sofia Martinez) — due 2026-10-07
- Run alpha sweep for batch autosizer with realistic p95 burst trace (Ben Gallagher) — due 2026-10-06
- Create sampling job for session-age histogram for top 5 customers (Maya Chen / Luis Ortega) — due 2026-10-07

Risk/communication plan:
- Customer-facing: outreach to the two impacted customers already in progress (CS looped in). If p99 spikes continue, we will restore kernel version on their serving clusters and schedule a postmortem.
- Internal: hold off on any wide-scale model rollouts that assume p50 improvements until kernel fallback is validated.

Notes for oncall:
- Alert SR-99 (preemption-rate) threshold temporarily lowered to 3% while kernel tests run. Oncall should escalate to Eng runtime leads if alerts persist for >15m.
- Tracing tag to inspect: runtime.kernel_path_version and kv.bucket_age. If both show frequent flips, collect a bundle and upload to the canary investigations channel.

Appendix (quick commands):
- Collect perf counters: ./tools/collect_perf.sh --host <host> --window 600 --out /tmp/prefetch_perf.tar
- Trigger segmented-KV snapshot: curl -X POST https://internal-api/kv/debug/snapshot?cluster=canary1
- Toggle kernel fallback: curl -X POST https://internal-api/runtime/config -d '{"kernel_fallback_window_s":60}'

End of midweek synthesis. Expect a follow-up doc after the overnight canary run (target 2026-10-07 AM).

metrics_snapshot: Canary cluster aggregated (24h): p50 latency 12.1ms, p95 42.7ms, p99 119ms; KV hit rate baseline 72.4% -> segmented-KV canary 75.6%; CPU % on impacted host: baseline 63% -> observed 78% during preemption spikes.
